_README: Opportunistic notes for FUTURE test work, captured while reading code (not a backlog of committed tests). Each entry: where it came from, what was observed, why it matters, and candidate tests. Append-only; promote items into tests/plan/backlog.tsv when scheduled.

notes.source: merge of origin/develop social-auth (AuthContext, WelcomeAuth/SocialProfile screens, server/social-auth-handler.ts)
notes.observation: Google + Apple sign-in were added with no test coverage. New users land in a social_auth_pending state and must complete a SocialProfileScreen (gender, date_of_birth) before the account is usable.
notes.why_it_matters: OAuth/native sign-in is hard to automate (system webviews, real accounts) but the pending->complete transition and the server token exchange ARE testable at the API layer.
candidate_tests: headless: social-auth-handler accepts a valid (mocked) Google idToken and creates a user with google_id set, social_auth_pending=true
headless: completing the social profile (gender + dob) flips social_auth_pending=false and issues a usable JWT
headless: an Apple idToken without email is accepted only for an existing apple_id (matches develop commit dbd7011)
e2e (entry-point only): the Google and Apple buttons render and are reachable on WelcomeAuthScreen

notes.source: implication of adding Apple Sign In
notes.observation: Adding 'Sign in with Apple' triggers App Store review requirements the app may not yet satisfy: (a) Apple's 'Hide My Email' relay must be handled (email may be a privaterelay.appleid.com address), (b) where any third-party login exists Apple requires Sign in with Apple be offered too (satisfied), (c) App Store now mandates in-app account deletion.
notes.why_it_matters: These are reviewer-blocking, not optional. The relay-email case affects emailHash uniqueness and any email-based dedup (server uses email_hash unique).
candidate_tests: headless: a privaterelay.appleid.com email is stored/hashed without colliding and without breaking duplicate-email detection
headless/e2e: in-app account deletion exists and actually deletes (or anonymizes) the user

notes.source: qa:provision drizzle-kit push during the merge reconcile
notes.observation: migrations/0009_add_social_auth_fields.sql creates PARTIAL unique indexes (users_google_id_unique ... WHERE google_id IS NOT NULL), but shared/schema.ts declares googleId/appleId with .unique() (a FULL unique constraint). drizzle-kit push therefore sees drift and wants to add a full constraint (prompting to truncate users).
notes.why_it_matters: The migration and the ORM schema definition disagree, so `drizzle-kit push` is not a no-op against a migration-built DB. This is a latent footgun for anyone using db:push and for the schema-drift gate baseline.
candidate_tests: infra: assert the migration-built schema and a drizzle-push schema converge (no pending drift) for the users uniqueness constraints
decision needed: standardize on partial vs full unique for google_id/apple_id and make migration + schema.ts agree

notes.source: mobile/src reading during recon (ExploreScreen, api.service.ts, AuthContext, crashReporter)
notes.observation: App assumes connectivity for all user data. Only the crash reporter has a NetInfo offline queue; there is no offline cache/queue for bubbles, events, or images. On network failure ExploreScreen renders a generic empty state (no offline messaging/retry) and images silently blank. AuthContext.refreshUser is the one graceful path (keeps cached profile).
notes.why_it_matters: User-reported: app is largely non-functional offline (bubbles you belong to vanish, icons missing). Out of scope to FIX now (characterize-state PR); these document current behavior so a fix can be regression-tested.
candidate_tests: characterization e2e/unit: with the network down, ExploreScreen shows an offline-distinct state (currently it does NOT) — mark known-fail until fixed
unit: api.service surfaces a typed offline error rather than a bare throw

notes.source: tests/e2e/auth/auth-0200-signup.yaml (this branch) vs the new signup screens
notes.observation: auth-0200 was updated to drive gender/DOB picker steps (button-select-gender, button-select-dob) that correspond to the new social-signup fields, but those testIDs are unverified against the merged WelcomeAuth/SocialProfile screens (native e2e deferred this session).
notes.why_it_matters: If the new screens lack those testIDs, the flow fails on selectors, not logic — exactly the 'mainly bad-selectors' category to triage when native e2e runs.
candidate_tests: verify (Maestro MCP) that button-select-gender / button-select-dob / input-name exist on the merged signup path before counting auth-0200 as a real failure

notes.source: P5 native-build sanity (`npm run type-check`) during the test-platform->develop merge
notes.observation: Root `tsc --noEmit` is GREEN; the mobile half (`cd mobile && tsc --noEmit`) FAILS. mobile/src/utils/crashReporter.ts is IDENTICAL to origin/develop (verified: no diff develop..HEAD; last touched by develop commits 864c62a + 1e3d6f1), so the errors are pre-existing on develop, NOT introduced by the merge. Errors are @sentry/react-native API drift: `Sentry.configureScope` was removed, `autoSessionTracking` renamed to `enableAutoSessionTracking`, plus a SpanExpiryEvent missing sessionId in crashReporter.test.ts. CI does not catch these (CI typechecks server/shared/client only, not mobile).
notes.why_it_matters: Type errors do not block Metro/native builds (Babel strips types), so the iOS/Android dev builds still compile; but the mobile app has untyped/incorrect Sentry calls that will no-op or throw at runtime (configureScope is undefined on the installed SDK). This is a develop bug surfaced by, not caused by, the merge.
candidate_tests: fix (separate PR against develop): migrate crashReporter.ts off removed Sentry APIs (configureScope -> Sentry.getCurrentScope()/withScope; autoSessionTracking -> enableAutoSessionTracking) and add sessionId to the test's SpanExpiryEvent fixtures
ci-gap: add a mobile `tsc --noEmit` job (allowed-to-fail or gated) so mobile type regressions are visible in CI

notes.source: stopping the P6 android e2e run with `python3 scripts/testctl.py nuke --nuke=qa,maestro,cli` during the test-platform->develop merge
notes.observation: `nuke --help` advertises `mcp` as a valid kill target (qa,cli,mcp,xcodebuild,headless,playwright,maestro,all|them-all), but nuke does not handle it: the command printed `Unknown nuke target(s) ignored: mcp` even though `mcp` was NOT in the list passed (qa,maestro,cli). Two distinct defects: (1) the `mcp` target is documented but unimplemented in the dispatch, so there is no working `testctl` way to kill a stray `maestro mcp` session; (2) a phantom `mcp` appeared in the 'ignored' warning when it was never requested, suggesting the target list is mis-parsed/expanded (likely `maestro` fans out to `maestro`+`mcp`, then `mcp` falls through as unknown). The qa runner's automatic kill of `maestro mcp` before iOS e2e still works; only the manual escape hatch is broken.
notes.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md's standing rule is that MCP Maestro and a CLI `maestro test` run fight over the singleton on-device XCUITest driver. The mitigation depends on being able to kill MCP. If an MCP session wedges a driver, an operator currently cannot clear it through the sanctioned tool (`testctl nuke mcp` is a no-op). Low urgency (auto-kill path covers iOS e2e), but a real gap in the documented tooling contract.
candidate_tests: fix: wire `mcp` into testctl nuke dispatch (pgrep/pkill the `maestro mcp` process) and reconcile target parsing so the 'ignored' warning only fires for genuinely unrequested targets
testctl self-test: assert every nuke target advertised in --help is actually handled (no documented-but-ignored targets)

notes.source: P6 native android e2e smoke (two runs) during the test-platform->develop merge; failure screenshots in tests/output/run-20260630t08{3001Z-566dd8,4519Z-dee674}
notes.observation: EVERY android smoke test fails at login-as.yaml step 1: after `reconnect-metro.yaml` runs (launchApp clearState -> openLink com.bubble.mobile://expo-development-client/?url=http://localhost:8081 -> wait), the `Assert "Log In" is visible` (60s) fails because the app never renders. Run 1 screenshot = blank white. Run 2 screenshot = the React Native RedBox: 'Unable to load script. Make sure you're running Metro or that your bundle index.android.bundle is packaged correctly for release', stack = loadJSBundleFromAssets -> loadScriptFromAssets -> loadJSBundle. So the dev client, after clearState wipes its stored Metro URL, is NOT reconnecting to Metro via the openLink deep link — it falls back to loading the bundle from ASSETS, which a dev build does not contain. Verified NOT caused by: (a) cold bundle build — a new metro-bundle gate pre-warmed it (HTTP 200 in 0.1s) and the failure persisted; (b) adb reverse — `adb reverse --list` shows tcp:8081 and tcp:3000 both forwarded; (c) the merge — root tsc green, ios `expo export` + android `index.bundle` both build clean, and headless/API smoke is 23/23.
notes.why_it_matters: This blocks ALL android native e2e (all flows start with login-as), so the 6/7 android baseline cannot currently be reproduced on this emulator. It is an Expo-dev-client reconnect fragility (the documented clearState-wipes-URL hazard), NOT a merge regression. The robust fix is release/embedded-bundle 'Mode B' (the bundle ships in assets, so loadJSBundleFromAssets succeeds and there is no Metro dependency or reconnect step at all).
candidate_tests: BUILD Mode B (native-device-tooling plan Phase 8): expo run:android --variant release with the embedded bundle; release flows in tests/e2e/release/ that DROP reconnect-metro.yaml; verify release-0100-launch-welcome passes where the dev-client smoke blanks

dev-mode investigation (if keeping dev client): does the openLink expo-development-client deep link actually set the dev-server URL on android? try re-issuing openLink with autoVerify, adding a post-openLink retry/poll for a known first-screen element, or asserting the dev-server URL was registered before proceeding
gate idea: after reconnect-metro, assert NOT the RedBox text 'Unable to load script' (fail fast + distinct message) instead of timing out 60s on the 'Log In' assert
